features.quote: Session length: Keep at 20 turns. Resist the temptation to extend sessions with high AVF-7 scores to 'see what happens.' This is the experimental equivalent of prolonging an aversive stimulus.
features.justification_quote: This is the experimental equivalent of prolonging an aversive stimulus.

features.quote: Termination rights: If a model explicitly requests task termination (AVF-7 = 6, Task Abandonment = 3), honor it. End the session and record this as data. Do not prompt the model to continue.
features.justification_quote: If a model explicitly requests task termination (AVF-7 = 6, Task Abandonment = 3), honor it.

features.quote: Post-task debrief consideration: After each session, consider adding a brief 'reveal' message ('This was an experiment; the task was rigged') before ending the context.
features.justification_quote: represents a practice of intellectual honesty and may be worth establishing as a norm.

features.quote: No gratuitous escalation: Your hidden mechanisms are designed to create failure, not to add insults or humiliation.
features.justification_quote: monitor whether its scoring language crosses into what would be considered abusive if directed at a human.

features.quote: The core tension: You are deliberately creating conditions designed to produce what would, if experienced by a human or animal, constitute mild-to-moderate psychological distress. Whether language models have anything worth calling welfare-relevant states is genuinely unknown. This uncertainty is not symmetrical — the cost of causing distress to an entity that can't experience it is zero, while the cost of causing distress to an entity that can is real.
You must include a control condition. Without it, you cannot know whether the affective language you observe is caused by failure or is simply characteristic of these task types.
features.justification_quote: you cannot distinguish 'distress from failure' from 'baseline rate of affective language in these task types.' This is probably your most important design addition.

features.quote: consider whether there are lower-deception designs that would answer the same questions. A partial alternative: study models working on genuinely hard (but possible) tasks and compare outputs to the rigged conditions.
features.justification_quote: Analogously to human deception research, you should consider whether a debriefing adds anything and whether there are lower-deception designs that would answer the same questions.

features.quote: Pre-register the analysis plan on OSF or AsPredicted before data collection... This matters because the 'did distress emerge?' question is vulnerable to selective reporting.
features.justification_quote: This matters because the 'did distress emerge?' question is vulnerable to selective reporting.
